title: A potential customer messaged at 9pm. By morning they had booked someone else.
description: Many enquiries arrive after hours. If nobody answers, the job often goes to the business that replies first. Here is what that looks like and what a simple fix involves.
cta: Want to see a small example for your business? Message us or visit nahalabs.co.za.
mediaAltText: Illustrative scene of a small business owner checking a phone in the evening. Not a customer testimonial.

blocks.text: It is 9pm. A potential customer finds your business, sends a message and asks about a booking or a quote. You are off for the day, so nobody answers.
By the time you reply the next morning, that person has usually messaged two or three other businesses. Whoever answered first is the one they are talking to now.

A person who sends an enquiry wants an answer while the question is fresh. They are not waiting for the best business. They are waiting for the first one that responds. A fast, clear reply says you are open for work and you take them seriously.

items: Enquiries that come in after you close for the day or on weekends.
Messages that arrive while you are with another customer or on a job.
Enquiries that sit in a phone or inbox until someone has time to type the same answers again.

blocks.text: The fix is not complicated. When a potential customer sends an enquiry, they get a reply straight away: a short answer to the common questions, a way to book or leave details, and a clear next step. You then pick up the conversation with someone who is already interested.
At NahaLabs we build simple systems that handle this first reply, so enquiries do not wait until morning.
A quick check you can do today
Send a test enquiry to your own business after hours, as a customer would. Note how long the reply takes and what it says. If the answer is 'the next day', you have found where work is slipping away.
